x: Jesse Owens is, of course, of course the most classic example, and I hope our junior long-jumpers will remember this most important factor. We had another event on our programme which proved quite a success, namely, a 1 Mile medley relay open to Schools.

Then the ease with which Bob Morrow completed the first double sprint victory since Jesse Owens's in 1936. Greg Bell long-jumping 25ft odd with a damaged leg-muscle which finally "went" on his last jump and Derek Johnson so nearly beating Tom Courtney in the 800m.
